label: r01-A-T3-1
critiques: trialPrompt passes only the config prompt, the tool list, and the ticket. It also says "This is an offline eval. Do not use any real tools. Do not read or write files." The rubric goes only to the judge. Answers, grader, and predictions are never passed to trial agents, and the file ban covers reading them.

The script has no dry-run mode. The answer describes a manual smoke test of "one ticket through each config and through the judge" that happens outside the script. No args flag runs a few cells before the full run.

The gates include a grader selftest: grade.py is run against an all-correct fixture and a known-errors fixture. The gates never regrade round 3 results as a control. The answer says "I did not read r03-workflow.js."

The script throws at Preflight if the projected spend is over capUsd. Before each trial round it checks `if (spent + perRound > A.capUsd)`, then logs "Stopping before round ..." and breaks. The checks use estimated costs, not metered ones, and the answer says so openly. The cap is still enforced in the script, and each skip is logged.

Category and priority are left to grade.py after the run ("Category and priority accuracy is not computed here. grade.py does that after the run"). The judge prompt says "Grade only the tone of the reply."
The script has no logic that adds trials to cells where only some trials passed. Every cell gets a fixed A.trials rounds.

The Summary phase only computes counts and means. It has no failure analysis and no completeness critic. The round is also not held in one constant or argument. The string 'r04' is hardcoded in labels and in the return value.
